**Indikator 15** is a specific clinical quality indicator tracked within the Danish healthcare system to monitor the outcomes of patients newly diagnosed with atrial fibrillation. Specifically, it measures the proportion of these patients who develop heart failure within one year of their initial diagnosis [^src1]. This metric is a central component of the [[atrieflimren-i-danmark|Atrieflimren i Danmark]] report published by the Regional Clinical Quality Improvement Program, which aims to evaluate and improve the treatment and monitoring of atrial fibrillation across the country [^src1].

By tracking this indicator, healthcare administrators and policymakers can identify variations in clinical practice and patient outcomes across different regions and health clusters. For the period spanning July 1, 2022, to June 30, 2023, the national average for Indikator 15 across [[danmark|Danmark]] was 6.1% (95% CI: 5.7–6.4) [^src1]. However, regional breakdowns reveal distinct variations; for instance, in [[klynge-vest|Klynge VEST]], the proportion of newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation patients who developed heart failure within a year was notably lower at 4.7% (95% CI: 2.6–8.0) during the same period [^src1]. These detailed, cluster-based figures serve as a vital tool for quality improvement and political governance within the Danish healthcare system.
